parameters.content:
## OPS.SLK-B · Slack Join Provisioner

Slack `team_join` event → verify signature → match email in `team_members` → resolve channels from `slack_role_channels` × `slack_market_slugs` → ids from `slack_channels` → (live only) invite, create the private rep channel for `sales_rep`, mark row `active`, welcome DM → `#ops-alerts`.

**Answer Slack first.** The Respond node fires before any Supabase or Slack call. Slack retries after 3 s otherwise and you get double provisioning. The URL-verification challenge is answered by the same node.

**Signature check is fail-closed.** `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` unset, timestamp older than 5 min, or HMAC mismatch → 401 and nothing runs. The HMAC is computed by the Crypto node (the Code sandbox cannot require('crypto')); the raw request body comes from the Webhook node's Raw Body option — do not turn it off.

**`SLACK_ONBOARDING_MODE`** — anything but `live` is shadow: full evaluation, then one `[SHADOW]` line in #ops-alerts naming exactly what would happen. No invites, no channel, no DB update. Flipping to live is Mark's separate decision.

**No role logic here.** Canvassers never see #dispatch because `slack_role_channels` has no such row, not because of an IF.

**Alerts you will see:** 🔴 UNKNOWN JOIN (no form row) · 🔴 DEPARTED REJOIN (row is departed, nothing provisioned) · 🟠 MISSING CHANNEL / NO ROLE MAPPING / UNKNOWN MARKET (data gaps, the rest still proceeds) · 🟠 REP CHANNEL … (create/lookup problem) · ✅ ONBOARDED.

**Idempotent-ish.** already_in_channel counts as success; name_taken on the rep channel falls back to finding it via conversations.list (Reece Bot must be a member to see a private channel).

`Resolve Channels` embeds `scripts/lib/slack-onboarding-resolve.js` verbatim — the test suite checks it.

nodes.name: Slack Events
nodes.notes: Raw Body ON — the HMAC needs the exact bytes Slack signed. The parsed JSON is still available as $json.body.

nodes.name: HMAC-SHA256
nodes.notes: The Code node cannot require("crypto") on this instance (module disallowed), so the HMAC is computed here. Verified 2026-09-08 against a locally signed request. The fallback secret only exists so an UNSET env var does not crash this node with "key must be a string"; Verify & Route still rejects the request (has_signing_secret=false), so it is fail-closed either way.

nodes.name: Is team_join?
nodes.notes: False = challenge answered, bad signature, some other event, or a bot user. Nothing else to do.

nodes.name: Lookup Member
nodes.notes: Always Output Data is ON so zero rows still reach the IF below as an empty item. Email was lower-cased on both sides (form and event).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $env.SLACK_OPS_ALERTS_CHANNEL_ID, text: '🔴 UNKNOWN JOIN · ' + ($('Verify & Route').first().json.email || '(no email on Slack profile)') + ' · Slack user ' + $('Verify & Route').first().json.slack_user_id + ' · no onboarding form on file' }) }}

nodes.name: Departed?
nodes.notes: A departed row must not be re-provisioned by a stray join. Alert and stop; Mark re-submits the form if the person is genuinely back.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $env.SLACK_OPS_ALERTS_CHANNEL_ID, text: '🔴 DEPARTED REJOIN · ' + $json.first_name + ' ' + $json.last_name + ' · ' + $json.email + ' · row is departed, nothing provisioned · re-submit the onboarding form if this is intended, then have them re-join' }) }}

nodes.name: Lookup Role Channels
nodes.notes: Role → channel rules are DATA in slack_role_channels. Zero rows here means the role has no mapping; the resolve node turns that into a 🟠 alert instead of failing.

nodes.name: Lookup Market Slug
nodes.notes: Company-wide people have market_code NULL → no row → slug "" → every <market> pattern is skipped.

nodes.name: Lookup Slack Channels
nodes.notes: Names → Slack channel ids. Any name with no row becomes a 🟠 MISSING CHANNEL alert downstream; the rest still proceed.

nodes.name: Live Mode?
nodes.notes: SLACK_ONBOARDING_MODE must be exactly "live". Unset, empty, "shadow", anything else = shadow.

nodes.name: Any Invites?
nodes.notes: Zero invites (every channel missing from slack_channels) must still reach Activate Member, so the loop is bypassed instead of stopping the run.

parameters.jsCode:
const plan = $('Plan Provisioning').first().json;
return plan.invites.map((i) => ({ json: { channel: i.id, name: i.name, users: plan.slack_user_id } }));

nodes.name: Invite to Channel
nodes.notes: One call per channel, 400 ms apart (Slack tier 3 = 50/min). Never Error is ON so already_in_channel and friends reach the collector instead of aborting the run.

nodes.name: Sales Rep?
nodes.notes: True only for role sales_rep WITH a market. Managers are NOT added to rep channels (decision: they see the same posts in the market channel).

nodes.name: Rep Channel In DB?
nodes.notes: slack_channels already has the rep row (re-onboarding) → skip creation, still set topic/purpose and invite.

nodes.name: Create Rep Channel
nodes.notes: Private. name_taken is handled by the next IF; any other error becomes a 🟠 alert and the person still gets activated without a rep channel.

nodes.name: List Channels
nodes.notes: Only reached on name_taken. Paginated; one output item per page. Reece Bot can only see private channels it is a member of — if the existing channel was made by hand, add the bot to it.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $('Rep Channel Id').first().json.rep_channel_id, topic: $('Plan Provisioning').first().json.first_name + ' ' + $('Plan Provisioning').first().json.last_name + "'s appointments and call summaries. Auto-posted." }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $('Rep Channel Id').first().json.rep_channel_id, purpose: 'Your personal channel. Reece Bot posts your appointments (set, confirmed, cancelled) and your call summaries here with the Lead Perfection link. Your manager sees the same posts in the market channel.' }) }}
={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $('Rep Channel Id').first().json.rep_channel_id, users: $('Plan Provisioning').first().json.slack_user_id }) }}

nodes.name: Record Rep Channel

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel_name: $('Plan Provisioning').first().json.rep_channel_name, slack_channel_id: $('Rep Channel Id').first().json.rep_channel_id, channel_type: 'rep', market_code: $('Plan Provisioning').first().json.market_code, member_id: $('Plan Provisioning').first().json.member_id }) }}

nodes.notes: Upsert on channel_name so re-onboarding the same rep does not 409.

nodes.name: Activate Member

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ slack_user_id: $('Plan Provisioning').first().json.slack_user_id, rep_channel_id: $('Rep Channel Id').isExecuted ? $('Rep Channel Id').first().json.rep_channel_id : null, status: 'active', activated_at: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: Reached from three places (not a rep / rep channel done / rep channel failed). Marks the row active even if some invites failed — those are 🟠 alerts in the summary, and re-running is safe.

nodes.name: Welcome DM
nodes.notes: Posting to a user id opens the DM (needs im:write). The dispatch sentence is only included when #dispatch is in the person's channel list — canvassers never get it.

meta.note: Ships INACTIVE. Activate BEFORE saving the Slack Event Subscription Request URL (https://n8n-main-instance-production-981e.up.railway.app/webhook/slack-events) — Slack verifies the URL immediately and this workflow must be live to answer the challenge. Runs in shadow mode (no Slack writes, no DB writes) until SLACK_ONBOARDING_MODE=live. See workflows/README-slack-onboarding.md.
